rows.proof: BOARD OF ASSESSORS, PDF page 10 of the FY2013 annual town report (printed page 7), the table headed `Assessor's Account for Exemptions and Abatements`. NO TEXT LAYER; read off the page's own 400 dpi bitmap. THE TABLE IS TRANSPOSED HERE -- each printed COLUMN is a row of this file, keyed by its fiscal year, and each printed ROW is a column -- because that is the grain the account runs in. ROW LABELS READ OFF THE PAGE AND NOT INFERRED (rule 13b.4), verbatim and in printed order: `Assessor's Overlay`, `Overlay Deficits`, `Charges to 6/30/2010`, `Potential Liability`, `Amount Released`. THE LABELS ARE NOT THE SAME AS THE FY2015 REPORT'S COPY of this table, which prints `Released to Surplus` and `Total Balance` where this one prints `Potential Liability` and `Amount Released`; the names are recorded as each document prints them. WHAT THE ARITHMETIC SHOWS. The account states one identity per fiscal year: the overlay raised plus any deficit raised equals the charges made against it, plus what is still potentially liable, plus what was released. FOUR OF THE FIVE YEARS CLOSE TO THE CENT -- FY2013 156,740.57 + 0.00 = 129,426.09 + 0.00 + 27,314.48; FY2012 141,918.23 = 112,691.50 + 29,226.73; FY2011 124,378.48 = 119,992.49 + 4,385.99; FY2009 97,988.20 + 30,209.07 = 128,197.27. FY2010 DOES NOT: 141,582.64 against 116,250.15 + 0.00 + 14,860.27 = 131,110.42, the DOCUMENT out by 10,472.22. Those digits were re-read at 400 dpi in a tight crop of the five printed rows and are the document's. WHY THIS GROUP IS CHECKED ON SHAPE AND NOT ON THAT IDENTITY. `verify_page_reads.py` expresses an identity as `a,b,c=d` (all added) or `a-b-c=d` (first added, rest subtracted). This account has TWO positive terms and three negative ones however it is rearranged, so NO supported form states it, and writing one of the five as `attested` to make a wrong form close would be attesting our own limitation as the town's error. So the declared check here is `cells_per_row` = 5: every fiscal year prints all five rows, `-0-` being the page's explicit zero and read as 0.00 rather than as an absent figure. THAT IS A WEAKER CHECK AND SAYS SO -- it proves the SHAPE of the read, not the digits. The arithmetic above is stated here, in full, so the next reader meets it. AND THE SAME LIMITATION IS LATENT IN `fy2015-p35-overlay.csv`, which declares `assessors_overlay-overlay_deficits-charges_to_063010-released_to_surplus=total_balance`: that puts a MINUS on overlay deficits, every one of that table's deficit cells is zero, and the sign has therefore never been tested. FY2009 here is the case that tests it, and it adds. A SECOND PRINTING, AND IT DISAGREES. The FY2015 annual town report prints this same account for FY2013 with `Charges to 6/30/2010` of 129,797.69 and a `Total Balance` of 26,760.88 -- neither figure is what this report prints, and that restatement does not close (it is already `attested` in fy2015-p35-overlay.csv, out by 182.00). THIS report's own FY2013 column closes exactly. Nothing here establishes which document is right about FY2013's charges; both are recorded as printed.

NO TEXT LAYER; read off the page's own 400 dpi bitmap. COLUMN NAMES READ OFF THE PRINTED HEADER (rule 13b.4), verbatim: `Property Class Code/Description`, `Accts`, `Class Valuation`, `Avg.Value`. THE CHECK: the page prints a `TOTALS` row and both summable columns tie EXACTLY -- 5,054 accounts and 1,131,029,744 of valuation, which is the same valuation the page's first table foots to across five statutory classes, so the page states the quantity twice by two different cuts and both readings agree. `average_value` is a per-account AVERAGE and not an addend: it has no printed total and the identity that would check it is multiplicative, which the verifier's identity grammar does not express. It is transcribed for coverage and NOTHING ASSERTS IT.

rows.reconciliation: page 10, the row `TOTALS`: percent 100.0 vs printed 100.0 ; tax_levy 19,566,814.57 vs printed 19,566,814.57 ; valuation 1,131,029,744.0 vs printed 1,131,029,744.0
rows.proof: BOARD OF ASSESSORS, PDF page 10 of the FY2013 annual town report (printed page 7). THE PAGE CARRIES NO TEXT LAYER -- every page of this report is a photograph -- so it was read off its own stored bitmap at 400 dpi, never recognised. COLUMN NAMES READ OFF THE PRINTED HEADER (rule 13b.4), verbatim: `Property Class`, `Levy Percent`, `Valuation by Class`, `Tax Rate`, `Tax Levy`. THE CHECK: the page prints a `TOTALS` row and all three summable columns tie to it EXACTLY -- levy percent 100.0000, valuation 1,131,029,744, tax levy 19,566,814.57. `tax_rate` is printed identically on every row and is not summable, so nothing asserts it. `-0-` is the page's explicit zero and is read as 0.00, never as an absent figure. TWO SECOND PRINTINGS AGREE: the same page's Abstract of Assessments reaches 1,131,029,744 by a different cut of the same base (twelve property class codes against five statutory classes, fy2013-p10-abstract.csv), and the FY2014 annual town report's own valuation history repeats this year's rate, valuation, account count and levy to the cent (fy2014-p35-valuation.csv, `history FY2013`). The levy is also the valuation at the printed rate: 1,131,029,744 x 17.30/1000 = 19,566,814.57, exactly. THE HISTORY AND NEW-GROWTH ROWS ARE `line`: they are a second table and a third table on the same page, neither of which prints a total, so they are transcribed and NOT summed. Their own internal regularity is recorded here rather than asserted: in the history table valuation x rate / 1000 reproduces the printed levy within $0.02 in all nine years (the two misses are FY2012 at $0.02 and FY2011 at $0.01, which is what rounding per bill produces), and in the new-growth table each `change_pct` is the ratio of its own `new_revenue` to the row BELOW it, within 0.01 of a point. `new_revenue` is NOT a clean product of `added_valuation` and the printed rate -- 2012 computes 321,861.21 against a printed 321,862 and 2010 computes 130,169.39 against a printed 130,170 -- so no identity is claimed for it. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, and it is a disagreement between two town documents rather than a reading: THE NEW-GROWTH YEAR LABELS ARE NOT SETTLED ACROSS REPORTS. This report heads the 19,124,255 row `2012`; the FY2014 report heads that same 19,124,255 row `FY2013`, and carries a 27,729,619 row (labelled FY2012 there) that this report does not print at all. Within this report the new-growth rate for a labelled year is the history table's rate for the year BEFORE it -- `2011` at 14.20 against a history FY2011 of 16.16. Both labellings are recorded as each document prints them and nothing here says which is right.

rows.proof: CAPITAL PLANNING, PDF page 12 of the FY2013 annual town report (printed page 9): the FY14 Plan as presented at the Annual Town Meeting of May 2013. NO TEXT LAYER; read off the page's own 400 dpi bitmap. COLUMN NAMES READ OFF THE PRINTED HEADER (rule 13b.4), verbatim: `DEPARTMENT`, `AMOUNT`, `ITEM`. THE CHECK: the page states its own total in the sentence ABOVE the table -- `the following items, totaling $ 523,483, were presented in the FY14 Plan` -- and the eleven printed amounts sum to 523,483 EXACTLY. The total is printed on this page, in prose rather than in a footing row, which is why searching a table for a `Total` row finds none (rule 13c). WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT: a capital PLAN presented to a town meeting, which is a proposal. It is not an appropriation and not an expenditure, and nothing here says any of these items was funded. The key of each row is the department and the item together, because the page prints four separate School Department rows and two Police Department rows and the department alone would collapse them.
